title: Listening practice: Before Class, a Book Club, and Cups of Water
description: Three clips to listen to twice: a short conversation, a book club discussion with claims, and two students arguing from test results.

stimuli.title: Listen: Before class

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Ravi, you look upset. What happened?

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: I missed the bus this morning. I ran after it, but the driver did not see me. Then my uncle drove me to school.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: You should tell Miss Lee why you were late. Telling the truth is a good idea, because then she will understand.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: Okay. I will tell her at the start of class.

stimuli.script: Sofia: Ravi, you look upset. What happened? Ravi: I missed the bus this morning. I ran after it, but the driver did not see me. Then my uncle drove me to school. Sofia: You should tell Miss Lee why you were late. Telling the truth is a good idea, because then she will understand. Ravi: Okay. I will tell her at the start of class.

stimuli.title: Listen: Book club

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Today we are talking about our story, The Lighthouse Girl. Who showed more courage, Nia or her brother Omar? Give a reason from the story.

turns.speaker: Jun
turns.text: I think Nia was braver. The storm knocked out the lamp, and Omar was too afraid to climb the stairs. Nia climbed all one hundred steps alone and lit the lamp by hand.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: I see it a little differently. Omar was afraid, but he was brave in another way. He stayed on the rocks and rang the warning bell so the ship would turn away from danger.

turns.speaker: Jun
turns.text: That is true, but Nia took the biggest risk. She went up alone while the wind shook the tower.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Thank you both. You each gave a claim and evidence from the story.

stimuli.script: Teacher: Today we are talking about our story, The Lighthouse Girl. Who showed more courage, Nia or her brother Omar? Give a reason from the story. Jun: I think Nia was braver. The storm knocked out the lamp, and Omar was too afraid to climb the stairs. Nia climbed all one hundred steps alone and lit the lamp by hand. Carmen: I see it a little differently. Omar was afraid, but he was brave in another way. He stayed on the rocks and rang the warning bell so the ship would turn away from danger. Jun: That is true, but Nia took the biggest risk. She went up alone while the wind shook the tower. Teacher: Thank you both. You each gave a claim and evidence from the story.

stimuli.title: Listen: Cups of water

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Our test is finished. I think the foil kept the water warmest, because foil is shiny and made of metal.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: I don't think so. Look at our numbers. All three cups started at fifty degrees Celsius. After twenty minutes, the water in the wool was forty-four degrees. The water in the foil was thirty-seven degrees, and the cup with no wrap was thirty-five degrees.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: So the water in the wool dropped the least?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Yes, it dropped only six degrees. The foil water dropped thirteen degrees, almost as much as the cup with nothing. So the wool kept the water warm best.

stimuli.script: Kofi: Our test is finished. I think the foil kept the water warmest, because foil is shiny and made of metal. Elena: I don't think so. Look at our numbers. The foil water dropped thirteen degrees, almost as much as the cup with nothing. So the wool kept the water warm best.

items.stem: How did Ravi get to school?

options.text: He ran after the bus all the way.
Sofia's mother drove him.
His uncle drove him.
He took the next bus.

distractors.a: Ravi ran after the bus, but the driver did not see him. Running did not get him to school.
distractors.d: Ravi does not say he took another bus.

items.explanation: Ravi says that after the driver did not see him, his uncle drove him to school.

support.clue: Listen for the word 'Then' near the end of Ravi's first turn. It tells the last thing that happened.
support.model: Mentor example. 'Mina missed the elevator. Then a neighbor gave her a ride to work.' The word then points to the last step. Listen for the last step in Ravi's story.

misconceptions.a: mixes up an attempt with the result
misconceptions.b: adds a detail that was not said
misconceptions.d: adds a detail that was not said

items.text: His uncle drove him to school.

items.explanation: Ravi missed the bus, ran after it, and then his uncle drove him to school.

support.clue: Listen to Ravi's first turn. He tells three things in the order they happened.
support.model: Mentor example. 'I dropped my pencil. I bent down to pick it up. Then the bell rang.' The events are told in the order they happened. Put Ravi's morning in order the same way.

items.stem: Why does Sofia say Ravi should tell the truth?

options.text: Miss Lee will understand why.
Ravi will not get a late slip.
The other students will not tease him.
His uncle will be proud of him.

distractors.b: Sofia never talks about a late slip. She says Miss Lee will understand.
distractors.c: Nobody in the talk mentions other students teasing Ravi.
distractors.d: Sofia never talks about how Ravi's uncle will feel. The uncle only drove Ravi to school.

items.explanation: Sofia says that telling the truth is a good idea because then Miss Lee will understand.

support.clue: Listen for the word 'because' in Sofia's second turn. The reason comes right after it.
support.frame: Sofia says Ravi should tell the truth because ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'You should drink water because it helps you stay healthy.' Advice usually has a reason after the word because. Listen for Sofia's reason.

misconceptions.b: adds a detail that was not said
misconceptions.c: adds a detail that was not said
misconceptions.d: adds a detail that was not said

items.stem: What is Jun's claim, and what is his main evidence?

options.text: Omar was braver, because he rang the warning bell.
Both were brave, because the storm was strong.
Nia was braver, because she rang the warning bell.
Nia was braver, because she climbed the tower alone.

distractors.a: This is Carmen's evidence for Omar, not Jun's claim.
distractors.b: Jun does not say both were equally brave. He says Nia was braver.
distractors.c: Jun's claim is right, but the warning bell is Omar's action.

items.explanation: Jun says Nia was braver because she climbed all one hundred steps alone and lit the lamp by hand.

support.clue: Listen to Jun's first turn. He says who he thinks was braver, and then gives a fact from the story.
support.model: Mentor example. 'I think the tortoise is the better hero because he never gave up, even when the path was long.' A claim and a reason are joined by the word because. Listen for Jun's claim and his reason.

misconceptions.c: attaches evidence to the wrong character

facts: The story The Lighthouse Girl and its characters are invented for this practice item.

items.stem: Match each speaker to what the speaker says.

right.text: Omar helped by ringing the warning bell.
Give a reason from the story.

items.explanation: Jun says Nia took the biggest risk by going up alone, Carmen says Omar rang the warning bell, and the teacher asks for a reason from the story.

support.clue: Listen for who says each idea. Jun speaks first and last among the students. Carmen speaks once.
support.model: Mentor example. 'Rosa says the park should open early. Sam says it should close late.' Name the speaker, then the idea. Match each speaker in the book club to the idea.

facts: The story The Lighthouse Girl and its characters are invented for this practice item.

items.stem: How does Carmen respond to Jun's claim?

options.text: She repeats Jun's idea and says Nia was braver.
She says Omar showed courage in a different way.
She says Omar was braver than Nia because of the storm.
She says Nia was brave but should not have gone alone.

distractors.a: Carmen begins by saying she sees it differently, so she does not just repeat Jun's idea.
distractors.c: Carmen says Omar was brave in another way. She does not say he was braver than Nia.
distractors.d: Carmen never says Nia should not have gone alone.

items.explanation: Carmen says Omar was afraid but brave in another way, because he rang the warning bell.

support.clue: Listen to Carmen's turn. She starts by saying whether she agrees. Then she adds a new idea.
support.frame: Carmen ______ with Jun's idea and adds that Omar ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'I like the blue poster. You like the red one, but the red one is also bright and neat.' A response can accept one idea and add another idea. Listen for how Carmen answers.

misconceptions.d: adds an opinion that was not said

facts: The story The Lighthouse Girl and its characters are invented for this practice item.

items.stem: Elena makes a claim about which cup kept the water warmest. Which fact supports her claim?

options.text: The foil is shiny and made of metal.
All three cups started at fifty degrees Celsius.
The wool water lost only six degrees.
The foil water lost fifteen degrees.

distractors.a: This is Kofi's reason for his own claim, not evidence for the wool.
distractors.b: This is true for all three cups, so it does not show that the wool is better.
distractors.d: Fifteen degrees is how much the cup with no wrap lost. The foil water lost thirteen.

items.explanation: The wool water dropped from fifty to forty-four degrees Celsius, only six degrees. That was less than the foil water or the cup with no wrap.

support.clue: Listen for Elena's numbers. Ask which number shows a cup changing the least.
support.frame: The ______ water dropped ______ degrees, which is ______ than the other cups.
support.model: Mentor example. 'Pia says the green plant grew the most. Her evidence: it grew nine centimeters and the red plant grew four.' Evidence uses numbers that match the claim. Listen for Elena's numbers.

misconceptions.b: uses a fact that is true of every cup

facts: Water that starts at 50 degrees Celsius in a cooler room cools over time.
The test results are invented for this practice item.

items.stem: Complete the sentence about the two claims.

dropdown.template: Kofi thinks the {1} kept the water warmest, but Elena says the {2} did.

items.explanation: Kofi says the foil kept the water warmest, and Elena uses the numbers to show the wool kept it warmest.

support.clue: Listen to who speaks first and what that speaker thinks. Then listen to Elena's two turns.
support.frame: Kofi thinks the ______, but Elena says the ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'Tess thinks the cat is hungry, but Jon says the cat is just sleepy.' Each speaker has a different idea. Match each idea to its speaker.

facts: The test results are invented for this practice item.
